newsitem.title: GERMANY: German beet test reflects weather improvements.
newsitem.headline: German beet test reflects weather improvements.

text.p: The third German sugar beet test result, published on Monday, reflects favourable weather patterns in August, an industry analyst said.
Sugar yield of 7.81 tonnes per hectare compared with 7.66 tonnes in the third test last year.
The first two tests of the year were down on 1995 levels, reflecting drought in the spring.
Sugar content of 15.3 percent compared with 15.5 percent a year ago, but in the second test a fortnight ago content was down one percentage point from last year at 15.0 percent.
"It could be a good year after all," the analyst said.
"Recent rainfall helped beet growth although it slowed sugar content development."
"Sunny weather may help even out these differences and produce a good crop, unless there are extraordinay changes."
Although slightly down from the second test, leaf weight of 648 grams versus 491 last year made the crop resistant to possible dry spells, the analyst added.
He also pointed to a plant density of 84,900 per hectare compared with 77,400 last year as a supportive factor for final sugar yields.
The latest sugar yield of 7.81 tonnes per ha compared with an average of 7.48 tonnes in western Germany's third test in the 1982-1995 period.
Sugar content of 15.3 percent was also up on the 1982-1995 average of 15.2.
Eastern German averages are available only from 1991.
The region's latest yield figure of 6.81 tonnes was above the 1991-1995 average of 6.67 tonnes, but sugar content of 15.3 percent lagged the four-year average of 15.7 percent.
Sugar industry association WVZ, which collects the national data, a week ago forecast sugar output in 1996/97 at 3.868 million tonnes, up 1.9 percent from 1995/96.
This was based on a 516,000 hectare 1996/97 beet area, up 0.5 percent from 1995/96.
The farm ministry last Thursday said sugar output could be lower than last year's, citing lower sugar content.

But the analyst believed sugar content was on its way to improvement, supporting WVZ expectations of a steady beet volume of 26 million tonnes and final sugar content of 17 percent versus versus 16.73 in the 1995/96 campaign.
Two more national tests are due over the next four weeks.
